questions.stem: The negation of statement pattern $(p \wedge \sim q) \rightarrow (p \vee \sim q)$ is
questions.solution:
Step 1: An implication $A \rightarrow B$ is false only when $A$ is true and $B$ is false.
Step 2: Here $A = p \wedge \sim q$. If $A$ is true then $p$ is true, so $B = p \vee \sim q$ is also true. Hence $A \rightarrow B$ is never false: it is a tautology.
Step 3: The negation of a tautology is false for every truth assignment, i.e. a contradiction.
Final Answer: (C) a contradiction
Quick Tip: $(p \wedge r) \rightarrow (p \vee s)$ is always a tautology, because the antecedent already forces $p$ to be true.

questions.stem: If the line $3x + 4y - 24 = 0$ intersects X and Y axes in points A and B respectively then incentre of the triangle OAB where O is origin is
questions.solution:
Step 1: Put $y = 0$: $A = (8, 0)$; put $x = 0$: $B = (0, 6)$. So $OA = 8$, $OB = 6$, $AB = \sqrt{64 + 36} = 10$.
Step 2: Triangle OAB is right-angled at O, so its inradius is $r = \frac{OA + OB - AB}{2} = \frac{8 + 6 - 10}{2} = 2$.
Step 3: The incircle touches both axes, so the incentre is $(r, r) = (2, 2)$.
Final Answer: (B) $(2, 2)$
Quick Tip: For a right triangle with legs on the axes, the incentre is $(r, r)$ with $r = \frac{a + b - c}{2}$.

questions.stem: The area of the triangle formed by the co-ordinate axes and a tangent to the curve $xy = a^{2}$ at the point $(x_{1}, y_{1})$ is ______ sq. units (where a, $x_{1}$ and $y_{1}$ are non-zero)
questions.solution:
Step 1: Tangent to $xy = a^{2}$ at $(x_{1}, y_{1})$: $xy_{1} + yx_{1} = 2a^{2}$, i.e. $\frac{x}{2x_{1}} + \frac{y}{2y_{1}} = 1$ (using $x_{1}y_{1} = a^{2}$).
Step 2: Intercepts on the axes are $2x_{1}$ and $2y_{1}$.
Step 3: Area $= \frac{1}{2}|2x_{1}||2y_{1}| = 2|x_{1}y_{1}| = 2a^{2}$.
Final Answer: (C) $2a^{2}$
Quick Tip: For a rectangular hyperbola $xy = c^{2}$, every tangent cuts off a triangle of constant area $2c^{2}$ with the axes.

questions.stem: The co-ordinates of the point in which line joining $(1, 1, 1)$ and $(2, 2, 2)$ intersects the plane $x + y + z = 9$ are
questions.solution:
Step 1: Direction of the line is $(2 - 1, 2 - 1, 2 - 1) = (1, 1, 1)$, so a general point is $(1 + t, 1 + t, 1 + t)$.
Step 2: Substitute in the plane: $3(1 + t) = 9 \Rightarrow t = 2$.
Step 3: Point $= (3, 3, 3)$.
Final Answer: (D) $(3, 3, 3)$
Quick Tip: Every point on this line has equal coordinates, so only $(3, 3, 3)$ can be the answer.

questions.stem: The minimum value of the slope of the tangent to curve $y = x^{3} - 3x^{2} + 2x + 93$ is
questions.solution:
Step 1: Slope $m(x) = \frac{dy}{dx} = 3x^{2} - 6x + 2$.
Step 2: $m'(x) = 6x - 6 = 0 \Rightarrow x = 1$, and $m''(x) = 6 > 0$, so this is a minimum.
Step 3: $m(1) = 3 - 6 + 2 = -1$.
Final Answer: (B) -1
Quick Tip: Write $3x^{2} - 6x + 2 = 3(x - 1)^{2} - 1$ to read off the minimum directly.

questions.stem: If $f(x) = \begin{cases} \frac{9^{x} - 2 \cdot 3^{x} + 1}{\log(1 + 3x) \cdot \tan 2x}, & \text{if } x \neq 0 \\ a(\log b)^{c}, & \text{if } x = 0 \end{cases}$ is continuous at $x = 0$, then $a + b + c =$
questions.solution:
Step 1: Numerator $9^{x} - 2 \cdot 3^{x} + 1 = (3^{x} - 1)^{2}$.
Step 2: $\lim_{x \to 0} \frac{(3^{x} - 1)^{2}}{\log(1 + 3x)\tan 2x} = \lim_{x \to 0} \frac{\left(\frac{3^{x} - 1}{x}\right)^{2}}{\frac{\log(1 + 3x)}{3x} \cdot \frac{\tan 2x}{2x} \cdot 6} = \frac{(\log 3)^{2}}{6}$.
Step 3: Continuity gives $a(\log b)^{c} = \frac{1}{6}(\log 3)^{2}$, so $a = \frac{1}{6}$, $b = 3$, $c = 2$.
Step 4: $a + b + c = \frac{1}{6} + 3 + 2 = \frac{31}{6}$.
Final Answer: (A) $\frac{31}{6}$
Quick Tip: Spot $9^{x} - 2 \cdot 3^{x} + 1$ as a perfect square $(3^{x} - 1)^{2}$ and use $\frac{a^{x} - 1}{x} \to \log a$.

questions.stem: If $x = \tan^{-1}\left\{\frac{\sqrt{1 + t^{2}} - 1}{t}\right\}, y = \cos^{-1}\left\{\frac{1 - t^{2}}{1 + t^{2}}\right\}$, then $\frac{dy}{dx}$ is equal to
questions.solution:
Step 1: Put $t = \tan\theta$: $\frac{\sqrt{1 + t^{2}} - 1}{t} = \frac{\sec\theta - 1}{\tan\theta} = \frac{1 - \cos\theta}{\sin\theta} = \tan\frac{\theta}{2}$, so $x = \frac{\theta}{2} = \frac{1}{2}\tan^{-1}t$.
Step 2: $\frac{1 - t^{2}}{1 + t^{2}} = \cos 2\theta$, so $y = 2\theta = 2\tan^{-1}t$ (for $t > 0$).
Step 3: $y = 4x \Rightarrow \frac{dy}{dx} = 4$.
Final Answer: (C) 4
Quick Tip: With $t = \tan\theta$ both expressions become multiples of $\theta$; then $\frac{dy}{dx}$ is just the ratio of the multiples.

questions.stem: Define $f(x) = \begin{cases} b - ax, & \text{if } x < 2 \\ 3, & \text{if } x = 2 \\ a + 2bx, & \text{if } x > 2 \end{cases}$ and if $\lim_{x \to 2} f(x)$ exists, then $\frac{a}{b} =$
questions.solution:
Step 1: Left-hand limit at $x = 2$: $b - 2a$. Right-hand limit: $a + 4b$.
Step 2: The limit exists, so $b - 2a = a + 4b \Rightarrow -3a = 3b \Rightarrow a = -b$.
Step 3: $\frac{a}{b} = -1$.
Final Answer: (B) -1
Quick Tip: Existence of a limit needs only LHL = RHL; the value $f(2) = 3$ is not used.

questions.stem: The function $f(x) = \sec\left[\log\left(x + \sqrt{1 + x^{2}}\right)\right]$ is______function
questions.solution:
Step 1: Let $g(x) = \log\left(x + \sqrt{1 + x^{2}}\right)$. Then $g(-x) = \log\left(\sqrt{1 + x^{2}} - x\right) = \log\frac{1}{x + \sqrt{1 + x^{2}}} = -g(x)$, so $g$ is odd.
Step 2: $f(-x) = \sec(g(-x)) = \sec(-g(x)) = \sec(g(x)) = f(x)$, since $\sec$ is even.
Final Answer: (A) even
Quick Tip: An even function of an odd function is even.

questions.stem: Derivative of $y = \sqrt{\sin x + \sqrt{\sin x + \sqrt{\sin x + \dots \infty}}}$ is
questions.solution:
Step 1: The expression repeats inside itself, so $y = \sqrt{\sin x + y}$, i.e. $y^{2} = \sin x + y$.
Step 2: Differentiate: $2y\frac{dy}{dx} = \cos x + \frac{dy}{dx}$.
Step 3: $\frac{dy}{dx}(2y - 1) = \cos x \Rightarrow \frac{dy}{dx} = \frac{\cos x}{2y - 1}$.
Final Answer: (D) $\frac{\cos x}{2y - 1}$
Quick Tip: For infinite nested radicals replace the tail by $y$ itself, square, then differentiate implicitly.

questions.stem: The feasible region for the constraints $x - y \geq 0, x - 5y \leq -5, x \geq 0, y \geq 0$ is shown by the figure:
questions.solution:
Step 1: $x - y \geq 0$ means $y \leq x$ (on or below the line $y = x$). $x - 5y \leq -5$ means $y \geq \frac{x + 5}{5}$ (on or above the line $x - 5y = -5$).
Step 2: The lines meet where $x = \frac{x + 5}{5} \Rightarrow x = y = \frac{5}{4}$. For $x > \frac{5}{4}$ the line $y = x$ lies above $y = \frac{x + 5}{5}$, so points between them exist only to the right of $\left(\frac{5}{4}, \frac{5}{4}\right)$.
Step 3: The feasible region is the unbounded wedge between the two lines starting at their intersection and opening to the right, in the first quadrant. This is figure (C).
Final Answer: (C) the unbounded wedge between the two lines to the right of their intersection
Quick Tip: Test a point: $(10, 5)$ satisfies both inequalities and lies in the wedge of figure (C), while the origin fails $x - 5y \leq -5$.

questions.stem: The area of the triangle whose vertices are $i, \omega$ and $\omega^{2}$ is (Where $\omega$ is a complex cube root of unity other than $1, i$ is an imaginary number)________ sq.units
questions.solution:
Step 1: The points are $i = (0, 1)$, $\omega = \left(-\frac{1}{2}, \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right)$, $\omega^{2} = \left(-\frac{1}{2}, -\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right)$.
Step 2: $\omega$ and $\omega^{2}$ lie on the line $x = -\frac{1}{2}$, so the base is $\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2} - \left(-\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right) = \sqrt{3}$.
Step 3: Height = distance of $(0, 1)$ from $x = -\frac{1}{2}$ $= \frac{1}{2}$. Area $= \frac{1}{2} \times \sqrt{3} \times \frac{1}{2} = \frac{\sqrt{3}}{4}$.
Final Answer: (D) $\frac{\sqrt{3}}{4}$
Quick Tip: $\omega$ and $\omega^{2}$ are conjugates, so the segment joining them is vertical; use base times height.

questions.stem: Three numbers are chosen at random from numbers 1 to 20 . The probability that they are consecutive is
questions.solution:
Step 1: Total ways $= {}^{20}C_{3} = \frac{20 \times 19 \times 18}{6} = 1140$.
Step 2: Consecutive triples are $(1, 2, 3), (2, 3, 4), \dots, (18, 19, 20)$: 18 triples.
Step 3: Probability $= \frac{18}{1140} = \frac{3}{190}$.
Final Answer: (C) $\frac{3}{190}$
Quick Tip: From $1$ to $n$ there are $n - 2$ sets of three consecutive numbers.

questions.stem: The approximate value of $\frac{1}{(2.002)^{2}}$ is
questions.solution:
Step 1: Take $f(x) = \frac{1}{x^{2}}$, $a = 2$, $h = 0.002$. Then $f'(x) = -\frac{2}{x^{3}}$.
Step 2: $f(2) = 0.25$ and $f'(2) = -\frac{2}{8} = -0.25$.
Step 3: $f(2.002) \approx f(2) + h f'(2) = 0.25 - 0.002 \times 0.25 = 0.25 - 0.0005 = 0.2495$.
Final Answer: (A) 0.2495
Quick Tip: The value must be slightly less than $0.25$; only 0.2495 fits.

questions.stem: The equation of plane passing through $(1, 0, 0)$ and $(0, 1, 0)$ and making an angle $45^\circ$ with the plane $x + y - 3 = 0$ is
questions.solution:
Step 1: A plane with x-intercept 1 and y-intercept 1 is $x + y + kz = 1$, normal $(1, 1, k)$.
Step 2: Angle with the plane $x + y - 3 = 0$ (normal $(1, 1, 0)$): $\cos 45^\circ = \frac{1 + 1}{\sqrt{2 + k^{2}}\sqrt{2}} = \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}$.
Step 3: $\frac{2}{\sqrt{2 + k^{2}}} = 1 \Rightarrow 2 + k^{2} = 4 \Rightarrow k = \pm\sqrt{2}$.
Step 4: Plane: $x + y \pm \sqrt{2}z - 1 = 0$.
Final Answer: (A) $x + y \pm \sqrt{2}z - 1 = 0$
Quick Tip: Check the given points first: options (B) and (D) are not satisfied by both $(1, 0, 0)$ and $(0, 1, 0)$.

questions.stem: The distance of the point $(5, 3, -1)$ from the plane passing through points $(2, 1, 0), (3, -2, 4)$ and $(1, -3, 3)$ is
questions.solution:
Step 1: Vectors in the plane: $(3, -2, 4) - (2, 1, 0) = (1, -3, 4)$ and $(1, -3, 3) - (2, 1, 0) = (-1, -4, 3)$.
Step 2: Normal $= (1, -3, 4) \times (-1, -4, 3) = (-9 + 16,\ -(3 + 4),\ -4 - 3) = (7, -7, -7) \parallel (1, -1, -1)$.
Step 3: Plane through $(2, 1, 0)$: $(x - 2) - (y - 1) - z = 0 \Rightarrow x - y - z - 1 = 0$.
Step 4: Distance $= \frac{|5 - 3 + 1 - 1|}{\sqrt{3}} = \frac{2}{\sqrt{3}}$.
Final Answer: (A) $\frac{2}{\sqrt{3}}$ units
Quick Tip: Verify the plane with the third point: $1 + 3 - 3 - 1 = 0$.

questions.stem: $\int \frac{dx}{\cos x(1 + \cos x)} =$
questions.solution:
Step 1: Partial fractions: $\frac{1}{\cos x(1 + \cos x)} = \frac{1}{\cos x} - \frac{1}{1 + \cos x}$.
Step 2: $\int \sec x\,dx = \log(\sec x + \tan x)$ and $\int \frac{dx}{1 + \cos x} = \int \frac{1}{2}\sec^{2}\frac{x}{2}\,dx = \tan\frac{x}{2}$.
Step 3: $\int \frac{dx}{\cos x(1 + \cos x)} = \log(\sec x + \tan x) - \tan\left(\frac{x}{2}\right) + c$.
Final Answer: (D) $\log(\sec x + \tan x) - \tan\left(\frac{x}{2}\right) + c$
Quick Tip: $1 + \cos x = 2\cos^{2}\frac{x}{2}$, so its reciprocal integrates to $\tan\frac{x}{2}$ (not $2\tan\frac{x}{2}$).

$\log(\sec x + \tan x) - 2\tan\left(\frac{x}{2}\right) + c$, where c is the constant of integration
$\log(\sec x + \tan x) + \tan\left(\frac{x}{2}\right) + c$, where c is the constant of integration
$\log(\sec x + \tan x) - \tan\left(\frac{x}{2}\right) + c$, where c is the constant of integration

questions.stem: Two cards are drawn successively with replacement from fair playing 52 cards. let X denote number of kings obtained when two cards are drawn, then $E(X^{2}) =$
questions.solution:
Step 1: With replacement, $X \sim B\left(2, \frac{1}{13}\right)$ since $P(\text{king}) = \frac{4}{52} = \frac{1}{13}$.
Step 2: $E(X) = np = \frac{2}{13}$, $\mathrm{Var}(X) = npq = 2 \times \frac{1}{13} \times \frac{12}{13} = \frac{24}{169}$.
Step 3: $E(X^{2}) = \mathrm{Var}(X) + [E(X)]^{2} = \frac{24}{169} + \frac{4}{169} = \frac{28}{169}$.
Final Answer: (D) $\frac{28}{169}$
Quick Tip: Option (A) is the variance; $E(X^{2})$ needs the extra $[E(X)]^{2}$.

questions.stem: The eccentric angle of the point $P(-6, 2)$ of the ellipse $\frac{x^{2}}{48} + \frac{y^{2}}{16} = 1$ is
questions.solution:
Step 1: $a = \sqrt{48} = 4\sqrt{3}$, $b = 4$; a point is $(a\cos\theta, b\sin\theta)$.
Step 2: $\cos\theta = \frac{-6}{4\sqrt{3}} = -\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}$ and $\sin\theta = \frac{2}{4} = \frac{1}{2}$.
Step 3: $\theta$ is in the second quadrant with these values, so $\theta = 150^\circ$.
Final Answer: (C) $150^\circ$
Quick Tip: Use both $\cos\theta$ and $\sin\theta$ to fix the quadrant of the eccentric angle.

questions.stem: If one of the diameters of the circle, given by the equation $x^{2} + y^{2} - 4x + 6y - 12 = 0$, is a chord of a circle, ' S ', whose centre is at $(-3, 2)$, then the length of radius of ' S ' is ______ units.
questions.solution:
Step 1: Given circle: centre $C_{1} = (2, -3)$, radius $r = \sqrt{4 + 9 + 12} = 5$.
Step 2: The diameter is a chord of S, and its midpoint is $C_{1}$. The line from the centre $C_{2} = (-3, 2)$ of S to the midpoint of a chord is perpendicular to the chord.
Step 3: $C_{1}C_{2}^{2} = (2 + 3)^{2} + (-3 - 2)^{2} = 50$. Radius of S: $R^{2} = C_{1}C_{2}^{2} + r^{2} = 50 + 25 = 75$.
Step 4: $R = \sqrt{75} = 5\sqrt{3}$.
Final Answer: (C) $5\sqrt{3}$
Quick Tip: Half-chord, distance to the chord and radius form a right triangle: $R^{2} = d^{2} + (\text{half chord})^{2}$.

questions.stem: The area of the region bounded by the parabola $y^{2} = 27x$ and the line $x = 1$ is _______ sq.units.
questions.solution:
Step 1: The region is symmetric about the X-axis: Area $= 2\int_{0}^{1} \sqrt{27x}\,dx = 2 \times 3\sqrt{3}\int_{0}^{1} x^{\frac{1}{2}}\,dx$.
Step 2: $\int_{0}^{1} x^{\frac{1}{2}}\,dx = \frac{2}{3}$.
Step 3: Area $= 6\sqrt{3} \times \frac{2}{3} = 4\sqrt{3}$.
Final Answer: (C) $4\sqrt{3}$
Quick Tip: Area cut from $y^{2} = 4ax$ by $x = h$ is $\frac{8}{3}\sqrt{a}\,h^{\frac{3}{2}}$; here $4a = 27$ gives $\frac{8}{3} \cdot \frac{3\sqrt{3}}{2} = 4\sqrt{3}$.

questions.stem: If $\sin(\alpha + \beta) = 1, \sin(\alpha - \beta) = \frac{1}{2}, \alpha, \beta \in \left[0, \frac{\pi}{2}\right]$, then $\tan(\alpha + 2\beta) \cdot \tan(2\alpha + \beta) =$
questions.solution:
Step 1: $\alpha + \beta = \frac{\pi}{2}$ and $\alpha - \beta = \frac{\pi}{6}$, so $\alpha = \frac{\pi}{3}$, $\beta = \frac{\pi}{6}$.
Step 2: $\alpha + 2\beta = \frac{2\pi}{3}$, $\tan\frac{2\pi}{3} = -\sqrt{3}$; $2\alpha + \beta = \frac{5\pi}{6}$, $\tan\frac{5\pi}{6} = -\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}$.
Step 3: Product $= (-\sqrt{3})\left(-\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}\right) = 1$.
Final Answer: (A) 1
Quick Tip: $(\alpha + 2\beta) + (2\alpha + \beta) = 3(\alpha + \beta) = \frac{3\pi}{2}$, and $\tan A \tan B = 1$ whenever $A + B$ is an odd multiple of $\frac{\pi}{2}$.

questions.stem: The value of $\int_{0}^{\pi} \left|\sin^{3} x\right| dx$ is
questions.solution:
Step 1: On $[0, \pi]$, $\sin x \geq 0$, so $\left|\sin^{3} x\right| = \sin^{3} x = \frac{3\sin x - \sin 3x}{4}$.
Step 2: $\int_{0}^{\pi} \sin x\,dx = 2$ and $\int_{0}^{\pi} \sin 3x\,dx = \frac{2}{3}$.
Step 3: Value $= \frac{1}{4}\left(3 \times 2 - \frac{2}{3}\right) = \frac{1}{4} \times \frac{16}{3} = \frac{4}{3}$.
Final Answer: (C) $\frac{4}{3}$
Quick Tip: $\int_{0}^{\pi} \sin^{3}x\,dx = 2\int_{0}^{\pi/2} \sin^{3}x\,dx = 2 \times \frac{2}{3}$ (Wallis).

questions.stem: The population $p$ of the city at time $t$ is given by $\frac{dp}{dt} = \frac{p}{2} - 100$. If initial population is 100 then $p =$
questions.solution:
Step 1: $\frac{dp}{dt} = \frac{p - 200}{2} \Rightarrow \frac{dp}{p - 200} = \frac{dt}{2}$.
Step 2: Integrate: $\log|p - 200| = \frac{t}{2} + C \Rightarrow p - 200 = Ae^{\frac{t}{2}}$.
Step 3: At $t = 0$, $p = 100$: $A = -100$. So $p = 200 - 100e^{\frac{t}{2}}$.
Final Answer: (B) $200 - 100e^{\frac{t}{2}}$
Quick Tip: Check $t = 0$ in the options: (A) gives 300, (B) gives 100, (C) gives 200, (D) gives 400; only (B) matches.

Step 1: Integrate by parts: $\int \log(x + 1)\,dx = (x + 1)\log(x + 1) - x$.
Step 2: $\left[(x + 1)\log(x + 1) - x\right]_{0}^{1} = (2\log 2 - 1) - (0 - 0)$.
Step 3: Value $= 2\log 2 - 1$.
Final Answer: (D) $2\log 2 - 1$
Quick Tip: Take the antiderivative of $\log u$ as $u\log u - u$ with $u = x + 1$.

questions.stem: If $A = \begin{bmatrix} a & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & b & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & c \end{bmatrix}$ where $a = 7^{x}, b = 7^{7^{x}}, c = 7^{7^{7^{x}}}$ then $\int |A|\,dx$, (Where $|A|$ is the determinant of the matrix $A$ ) is equal to
questions.solution:
Step 1: $|A| = abc = 7^{x} \cdot 7^{7^{x}} \cdot 7^{7^{7^{x}}}$ (diagonal matrix).
Step 2: Let $u = 7^{7^{7^{x}}}$. By the chain rule, $\frac{du}{dx} = 7^{7^{7^{x}}}\log 7 \cdot 7^{7^{x}}\log 7 \cdot 7^{x}\log 7 = abc(\log 7)^{3}$.
Step 3: So $\int abc\,dx = \int \frac{du}{(\log 7)^{3}} = \frac{7^{7^{7^{x}}}}{(\log 7)^{3}} + k$.
Final Answer: (C) $\frac{7^{7^{7^{x}}}}{(\log 7)^{3}} + k$
Quick Tip: The integrand is exactly the derivative of the top tower divided by $(\log 7)^{3}$, one $\log 7$ per level.

options.text: $\frac{7^{7^{x}}}{(\log 7)^{3}} + k$, where k is constant of integration
$\frac{7^{7^{7^{x}}}}{\log 7} + k$, where k is constant of integration
$\frac{7^{7^{7^{x}}}}{(\log 7)^{3}} + k$, where k is constant of integration
$7^{7^{7^{x}}}(\log 7)^{3} + k$, where k is constant of integration

questions.stem: $\int \frac{\sin 7x}{\cos 9x \cos 2x}\,dx$ is equal to
questions.solution:
Step 1: $\sin 7x = \sin(9x - 2x) = \sin 9x\cos 2x - \cos 9x\sin 2x$.
Step 2: So $\frac{\sin 7x}{\cos 9x\cos 2x} = \tan 9x - \tan 2x$.
Step 3: $\int(\tan 9x - \tan 2x)\,dx = \frac{1}{9}\log\sec(9x) - \frac{1}{2}\log\sec(2x) + c$.
Final Answer: (C) $\frac{1}{9}\log\sec(9x) - \frac{1}{2}\log\sec(2x) + c$
Quick Tip: When the numerator angle is the difference of the two denominator angles, split into a difference of tangents.

options.text: $\log\sec(9x) - \log\sec(2x) + c$, where c is the constant of integration
$\log\sec(9x) + \log\sec(2x) + c$, where c is the constant of integration
$\frac{1}{9}\log\sec(9x) - \frac{1}{2}\log\sec(2x) + c$, where c is the constant of integration

questions.stem: The solution of the equation $\frac{dy}{dx} = \frac{1}{x + y + 1}$ is
questions.solution:
Step 1: Invert: $\frac{dx}{dy} = x + y + 1$, i.e. $\frac{dx}{dy} - x = y + 1$, linear in $x$ with I.F. $= e^{-y}$.
Step 2: $xe^{-y} = \int (y + 1)e^{-y}\,dy = -(y + 1)e^{-y} - e^{-y} + C = -(y + 2)e^{-y} + C$.
Step 3: $x = -(y + 2) + Ce^{y} \Rightarrow x + y + 2 = Ce^{y}$.
Step 4: Taking logs: $y = \log(x + y + 2) + c$.
Final Answer: (C) $y = \log(x + y + 2) + c$
Quick Tip: Alternatively put $v = x + y + 1$: $\frac{dv}{dx} = \frac{v + 1}{v}$ separates directly.

$x = \log(x + y - 2) + c$, where c is the constant of integration
$y = \log(x + y + 2) + c$, where c is the constant of integration

questions.stem: A spherical balloon is filled with $4500\pi$ cubic meters of helium gas. If a leak in the balloon causes the gas to escape at the rate of $72\pi$ cubic meters per minute, then the rate (in meters per minute) at which the radius of the balloon decreases 49 minutes after the leakage has begun, is
questions.solution:
Step 1: Volume after 49 min: $V = 4500\pi - 72\pi \times 49 = 4500\pi - 3528\pi = 972\pi$.
Step 2: $\frac{4}{3}\pi r^{3} = 972\pi \Rightarrow r^{3} = 729 \Rightarrow r = 9$ m.
Step 3: $\frac{dV}{dt} = 4\pi r^{2}\frac{dr}{dt} = -72\pi \Rightarrow \frac{dr}{dt} = -\frac{72}{4 \times 81} = -\frac{2}{9}$.
Step 4: The radius decreases at the rate of $\frac{2}{9}$ m per minute.
Final Answer: (D) $\frac{2}{9}$
Quick Tip: The question asks for the rate of decrease, so report the magnitude; $-\frac{2}{9}$ is the rate of change.

questions.stem: If $x \cdot \log_{e}(\log_{e} x) - x^{2} + y^{2} = 4\ (y > 0)$, then $\frac{dy}{dx}$ at $x = e$ is
questions.solution:
Step 1: At $x = e$: $\log_{e}(\log_{e} e) = \log 1 = 0$, so $y^{2} = 4 + e^{2}$, $y = \sqrt{4 + e^{2}}$.
Step 2: Differentiate: $\log(\log x) + x \cdot \frac{1}{x\log x} - 2x + 2y\frac{dy}{dx} = 0$.
Step 3: At $x = e$: $0 + 1 - 2e + 2\sqrt{4 + e^{2}}\frac{dy}{dx} = 0 \Rightarrow \frac{dy}{dx} = \frac{2e - 1}{2\sqrt{4 + e^{2}}}$.
Final Answer: (B) $\frac{2e - 1}{2\sqrt{4 + e^{2}}}$
Quick Tip: Find $y$ at the point first; $\log(\log e) = 0$ simplifies everything.

questions.stem: If p : switch $S_{1}$ is closed, q : switch $S_{2}$ is closed then correct interpretation from the following circuit is
questions.solution:
Step 1: $S_{1}$, the parallel block of $S_{1}'$ and $S_{2}'$, and $S_{2}$ are in series. $S_{1}' \equiv \sim p$, $S_{2}' \equiv \sim q$, so the circuit is $p \wedge (\sim p \vee \sim q) \wedge q$.
Step 2: $p \wedge q \wedge (\sim p \vee \sim q) = (p \wedge q) \wedge \sim(p \wedge q)$, which is always false (a contradiction).
Step 3: So current never flows: the lamp is always off.
Final Answer: (B) The lamp is always off
Quick Tip: Series = $\wedge$, parallel = $\vee$; $X \wedge \sim X$ is always false.

options.text: Symbolic form is $p \vee (\sim p \wedge \sim q) \vee q$

questions.stem: The solution of $\log\left(\frac{dy}{dx}\right) = 2x - 5y, y(0) = 0$ is
questions.solution:
Step 1: $\frac{dy}{dx} = e^{2x - 5y} \Rightarrow e^{5y}\,dy = e^{2x}\,dx$.
Step 2: Integrate: $\frac{e^{5y}}{5} = \frac{e^{2x}}{2} + C$.
Step 3: $y(0) = 0$: $\frac{1}{5} = \frac{1}{2} + C \Rightarrow C = -\frac{3}{10}$.
Step 4: Multiply by 10: $2e^{5y} = 5e^{2x} - 3 \Rightarrow 5e^{2x} - 2e^{5y} = 3$.
Final Answer: (B) $5e^{2x} - 2e^{5y} = 3$
Quick Tip: Check $x = y = 0$ in the options: only (B) gives $5 - 2 = 3$.

questions.stem: The integrating factor of the differential equation $x\frac{dy}{dx} + y\log x = x \cdot e^{x} x^{-\frac{1}{2}} \log x\ (x > 0)$ is
questions.solution:
Step 1: Divide by $x$: $\frac{dy}{dx} + \frac{\log x}{x}y = Q(x)$, so $P = \frac{\log x}{x}$.
Step 2: $\int P\,dx = \int \frac{\log x}{x}\,dx = \frac{(\log x)^{2}}{2}$.
Step 3: I.F. $= e^{\frac{(\log x)^{2}}{2}} = \left(e^{\log x}\right)^{\frac{\log x}{2}} = x^{\frac{\log x}{2}} = (\sqrt{x})^{\log x}$.
Final Answer: (C) $(\sqrt{x})^{\log x}$
Quick Tip: The I.F. depends only on the coefficient of $y$; the right-hand side does not matter.

questions.stem: ABCD is a quadrilateral with $\overline{AB} = \bar{a}, \overline{AD} = \bar{b}$ and $\overline{AC} = 2\bar{a} + 3\bar{b}$. If its area is $\alpha$ times the area of the parallelogram with $AB, AD$ as adjacent sides, then the value of $\alpha$ is
questions.solution:
Step 1: Area of a quadrilateral $= \frac{1}{2}\left|\overline{AC} \times \overline{BD}\right|$, with $\overline{BD} = \bar{b} - \bar{a}$.
Step 2: $(2\bar{a} + 3\bar{b}) \times (\bar{b} - \bar{a}) = 2\bar{a} \times \bar{b} - 3\bar{b} \times \bar{a} = 2\bar{a} \times \bar{b} + 3\bar{a} \times \bar{b} = 5\bar{a} \times \bar{b}$.
Step 3: Area of ABCD $= \frac{5}{2}|\bar{a} \times \bar{b}|$, while the parallelogram area is $|\bar{a} \times \bar{b}|$. So $\alpha = \frac{5}{2}$.
Final Answer: (B) $\frac{5}{2}$
Quick Tip: Area of any quadrilateral is half the magnitude of the cross product of its diagonals.

questions.stem: The equation of a line passing through the point $(-1, 2, 3)$ and perpendicular to the lines $\frac{x}{2} = \frac{y - 1}{-3} = \frac{z + 2}{-2}$ and $\frac{x + 3}{-1} = \frac{y + 3}{2} = \frac{z - 1}{3}$ is
questions.solution:
Step 1: Direction ratios of the given lines: $(2, -3, -2)$ and $(-1, 2, 3)$.
Step 2: Required direction $= (2, -3, -2) \times (-1, 2, 3) = (-9 + 4,\ -(6 - 2),\ 4 - 3) = (-5, -4, 1) \parallel (5, 4, -1)$.
Step 3: Line through $(-1, 2, 3)$: $\frac{x + 1}{5} = \frac{y - 2}{4} = \frac{z - 3}{-1}$.
Final Answer: (C) $\frac{x + 1}{5} = \frac{y - 2}{4} = \frac{z - 3}{-1}$
Quick Tip: Check perpendicularity: $(5, 4, -1) \cdot (2, -3, -2) = 10 - 12 + 2 = 0$ and $(5, 4, -1) \cdot (-1, 2, 3) = -5 + 8 - 3 = 0$.

questions.stem: If $A = \begin{bmatrix} 1 & -2 & 2 \\ 0 & 2 & -3 \\ 3 & -2 & 4 \end{bmatrix}$ then $A(I + \operatorname{adj} A) =$
questions.solution:
Step 1: $A(I + \operatorname{adj} A) = A + A\operatorname{adj} A = A + |A|I$.
Step 2: $|A| = 1(8 - 6) - (-2)(0 + 9) + 2(0 - 6) = 2 + 18 - 12 = 8$.
Step 3: $A + 8I = \begin{bmatrix} 9 & -2 & 2 \\ 0 & 10 & -3 \\ 3 & -2 & 12 \end{bmatrix}$.
Final Answer: (C) $\begin{bmatrix} 9 & -2 & 2 \\ 0 & 10 & -3 \\ 3 & -2 & 12 \end{bmatrix}$
Quick Tip: $A \cdot \operatorname{adj} A = |A|I$, so only the diagonal of $A$ changes (each by $|A|$).

questions.stem: A line L is passing through points $A(1, 3, 2)$ and $B(2, 2, 1)$. If mirror image of point $P(1, 1, -1)$ in the line L is $(x, y, z)$ then $x + y + z =$
questions.solution:
Step 1: Direction of L: $(1, -1, -1)$; general point $M = (1 + t, 3 - t, 2 - t)$.
Step 2: $\overrightarrow{MP} = (-t, -2 + t, -3 + t)$. Foot of perpendicular: $\overrightarrow{MP} \cdot (1, -1, -1) = -t + 2 - t + 3 - t = 5 - 3t = 0 \Rightarrow t = \frac{5}{3}$, so $M = \left(\frac{8}{3}, \frac{4}{3}, \frac{1}{3}\right)$.
Step 3: Image $= 2M - P = \left(\frac{16}{3} - 1, \frac{8}{3} - 1, \frac{2}{3} + 1\right) = \left(\frac{13}{3}, \frac{5}{3}, \frac{5}{3}\right)$.
Step 4: $x + y + z = \frac{13 + 5 + 5}{3} = \frac{23}{3}$.
Final Answer: (D) $\frac{23}{3}$
Quick Tip: Image of P in a line = $2 \times$ (foot of perpendicular) $- P$.

questions.stem: If $\bar{c} = 5\bar{a} + 6\bar{b}$ and $3\bar{c} = \bar{a} - 4\bar{b}$ then
questions.solution:
Step 1: $3\bar{c} = 15\bar{a} + 18\bar{b} = \bar{a} - 4\bar{b} \Rightarrow 14\bar{a} = -22\bar{b} \Rightarrow \bar{a} = -\frac{11}{7}\bar{b}$. So $\bar{a}$ and $\bar{b}$ are in opposite directions.
Step 2: $\bar{b} = -\frac{7}{11}\bar{a}$, so $\bar{c} = 5\bar{a} - \frac{42}{11}\bar{a} = \frac{13}{11}\bar{a}$. So $\bar{c}$ and $\bar{a}$ are in the same direction.
Final Answer: (C) $\bar{a}, \bar{c}$ are in the same direction but $\bar{a}, \bar{b}$ are in the opposite direction
Quick Tip: Eliminate $\bar{c}$ first to get the relation between $\bar{a}$ and $\bar{b}$, then express $\bar{c}$ in terms of $\bar{a}$; the sign of the scalar gives the direction.

options.text: $\bar{a}, \bar{c}$ are in the same direction but $\bar{a}, \bar{b}$ are in the opposite direction

questions.stem: The equation $x^{2} - 3xy + 2y^{2} + 3x - 5y + 2 = 0$ represents a pair of straight lines. If $\theta$ is the angle between them, then the value of $\cos\theta$ is equal to
questions.solution:
Step 1: Here $a = 1$, $2h = -3$, $b = 2$. $\tan\theta = \left|\frac{2\sqrt{h^{2} - ab}}{a + b}\right| = \frac{2\sqrt{\frac{9}{4} - 2}}{3} = \frac{2 \times \frac{1}{2}}{3} = \frac{1}{3}$.
Step 2: $\cos\theta = \frac{1}{\sqrt{1 + \tan^{2}\theta}} = \frac{1}{\sqrt{1 + \frac{1}{9}}} = \frac{3}{\sqrt{10}}$.
Final Answer: (B) $\frac{3}{\sqrt{10}}$
Quick Tip: Directly, $\cos\theta = \frac{|a + b|}{\sqrt{(a - b)^{2} + 4h^{2}}} = \frac{3}{\sqrt{1 + 9}} = \frac{3}{\sqrt{10}}$.

Step 1: $\cot^{-1}(2n^{2}) = \tan^{-1}\frac{1}{2n^{2}} = \tan^{-1}\frac{2}{4n^{2}} = \tan^{-1}\frac{(2n + 1) - (2n - 1)}{1 + (2n + 1)(2n - 1)}$.
Step 2: So each term is $\tan^{-1}(2n + 1) - \tan^{-1}(2n - 1)$, and the sum of $n$ terms telescopes to $\tan^{-1}(2n + 1) - \tan^{-1}1$.
Step 3: As $n \to \infty$: $\frac{\pi}{2} - \frac{\pi}{4} = \frac{\pi}{4}$.
Final Answer: (C) $\frac{\pi}{4}$
Quick Tip: Multiply numerator and denominator by 2 to write $\frac{2}{1 + (4n^{2} - 1)}$ and spot the telescoping difference.

questions.stem: With usual notation, in a triangle ABC $\frac{b + c}{11} = \frac{c + a}{12} = \frac{a + b}{13}$, then the value of $\cos B$ is equal to
questions.solution:
Step 1: Let $b + c = 11k$, $c + a = 12k$, $a + b = 13k$. Adding: $a + b + c = 18k$, so $a = 7k$, $b = 6k$, $c = 5k$.
Step 2: $\cos B = \frac{a^{2} + c^{2} - b^{2}}{2ac} = \frac{49 + 25 - 36}{2 \times 7 \times 5} = \frac{38}{70}$.
Step 3: $\cos B = \frac{19}{35}$.
Final Answer: (C) $\frac{19}{35}$
Quick Tip: Each side = (half the total) minus the sum given for the other two sides.

questions.stem: If $\bar{a} = \frac{1}{\sqrt{10}}(3\hat{i} + \hat{k}), \bar{b} = \frac{1}{7}(2\hat{i} + 3\hat{j} - 6\hat{k})$, then the value of $(\bar{a} - 2\bar{b}) \cdot \{(\bar{a} \times \bar{b}) \times (2\bar{a} + \bar{b})\}$ is
questions.solution:
Step 1: $|\bar{a}| = \frac{\sqrt{9 + 1}}{\sqrt{10}} = 1$, $|\bar{b}| = \frac{\sqrt{4 + 9 + 36}}{7} = 1$, $\bar{a} \cdot \bar{b} = \frac{6 + 0 - 6}{7\sqrt{10}} = 0$. Hence $|\bar{a} \times \bar{b}| = 1$.
Step 2: Let $\bar{u} = \bar{a} \times \bar{b}$. The expression is the box product $[\bar{a} - 2\bar{b}\ \ \bar{u}\ \ 2\bar{a} + \bar{b}] = \bar{u} \cdot \{(2\bar{a} + \bar{b}) \times (\bar{a} - 2\bar{b})\}$.
Step 3: $(2\bar{a} + \bar{b}) \times (\bar{a} - 2\bar{b}) = -4\bar{a} \times \bar{b} + \bar{b} \times \bar{a} = -5\bar{u}$.
Step 4: Value $= \bar{u} \cdot (-5\bar{u}) = -5|\bar{a} \times \bar{b}|^{2} = -5$.
Final Answer: (B) -5
Quick Tip: $\bar{p} \cdot (\bar{u} \times \bar{q}) = \bar{u} \cdot (\bar{q} \times \bar{p})$ (cyclic box product) turns this into a multiple of $|\bar{a} \times \bar{b}|^{2}$.

questions.stem: The vectors $\bar{p} = \hat{i} + a\hat{j} + a^{2}\hat{k}, \bar{q} = \hat{i} + b\hat{j} + b^{2}\hat{k}$ and $\bar{r} = \hat{i} + c\hat{j} + c^{2}\hat{k}$ are non-coplanar and $\begin{vmatrix} a & a^{2} & 1 + a^{3} \\ b & b^{2} & 1 + b^{3} \\ c & c^{2} & 1 + c^{3} \end{vmatrix} = 0$ then the value of $(abc)$ is
questions.solution:
Step 1: Split the third column: $\begin{vmatrix} a & a^{2} & 1 \\ b & b^{2} & 1 \\ c & c^{2} & 1 \end{vmatrix} + \begin{vmatrix} a & a^{2} & a^{3} \\ b & b^{2} & b^{3} \\ c & c^{2} & c^{3} \end{vmatrix} = 0$.
Step 2: Let $D = \begin{vmatrix} 1 & a & a^{2} \\ 1 & b & b^{2} \\ 1 & c & c^{2} \end{vmatrix}$. Moving the last column to the front (two swaps) makes the first determinant $D$; taking $a, b, c$ out of the rows makes the second $abc\,D$.
Step 3: So $(1 + abc)D = 0$. Since $\bar{p}, \bar{q}, \bar{r}$ are non-coplanar, $D = [\bar{p}\ \bar{q}\ \bar{r}] \neq 0$.
Step 4: Hence $1 + abc = 0 \Rightarrow abc = -1$.
Final Answer: (B) -1
Quick Tip: Non-coplanar means the scalar triple product (the Vandermonde determinant here) is non-zero, so the other factor must vanish.

questions.stem: Two adjacent sides of a parallelogram $ABCD$ are given by $\overline{AB} = 2\hat{i} + 10\hat{j} + 11\hat{k}$ and $\overline{AD} = -\hat{i} + 2\hat{j} + 2\hat{k}$. The side AD is rotated by an acute angle $\alpha$ in the plane of parallelogram so that AD becomes $AD'$. If $AD'$ makes a right angle with the side AB , then $\cos\alpha =$
questions.solution:
Step 1: $|\overline{AB}| = \sqrt{4 + 100 + 121} = 15$, $|\overline{AD}| = \sqrt{1 + 4 + 4} = 3$, $\overline{AB} \cdot \overline{AD} = -2 + 20 + 22 = 40$.
Step 2: Angle $\theta$ between AB and AD: $\cos\theta = \frac{40}{15 \times 3} = \frac{8}{9}$ (acute).
Step 3: Rotating AD by $\alpha$ in the same plane makes the angle with AB equal to $90^\circ$, so $\alpha = 90^\circ - \theta$ and $\cos\alpha = \sin\theta = \sqrt{1 - \frac{64}{81}} = \frac{\sqrt{17}}{9}$.
Final Answer: (B) $\frac{\sqrt{17}}{9}$
Quick Tip: The rotation angle is the complement of the original angle, so $\cos\alpha = \sin\theta$.

questions.stem: The general solutions of the equation $\tan^{2}\theta + \sec 2\theta = 1$ are
questions.solution:
Step 1: Let $t = \tan^{2}\theta$. Then $\sec 2\theta = \frac{1 + t}{1 - t}$.
Step 2: $t + \frac{1 + t}{1 - t} = 1 \Rightarrow t(1 - t) + 1 + t = 1 - t \Rightarrow 3t - t^{2} = 0 \Rightarrow t = 0$ or $t = 3$.
Step 3: $\tan\theta = 0 \Rightarrow \theta = n\pi$; $\tan^{2}\theta = 3 = \tan^{2}\frac{\pi}{3} \Rightarrow \theta = n\pi \pm \frac{\pi}{3}$.
Final Answer: (A) $n\pi, n\pi \pm \frac{\pi}{3}, n \in \mathbb{Z}$
Quick Tip: Express $\sec 2\theta$ through $\tan^{2}\theta$ to get a quadratic in $\tan^{2}\theta$.

questions.stem: In a triangle $ABC$, with usual notations, the sides a, b, c are such that they are roots of the equation $x^{3} - 11x^{2} + 38x - 40 = 0$ then $\frac{\cos A}{a} + \frac{\cos B}{b} + \frac{\cos C}{c} =$
questions.solution:
Step 1: $\frac{\cos A}{a} = \frac{b^{2} + c^{2} - a^{2}}{2abc}$, etc. Adding: $\sum\frac{\cos A}{a} = \frac{a^{2} + b^{2} + c^{2}}{2abc}$.
Step 2: From the cubic: $a + b + c = 11$, $ab + bc + ca = 38$, $abc = 40$. So $a^{2} + b^{2} + c^{2} = 121 - 76 = 45$.
Step 3: Value $= \frac{45}{2 \times 40} = \frac{9}{16}$.
Final Answer: (A) $\frac{9}{16}$
Quick Tip: The roots are $2, 4, 5$; you can also check $\frac{4 + 16 + 25}{80} = \frac{9}{16}$ directly.

questions.stem: The value of $\tan\left[2\tan^{-1}\frac{1}{5} - \frac{\pi}{4}\right]$ is
questions.solution:
Step 1: $2\tan^{-1}\frac{1}{5} = \tan^{-1}\frac{\frac{2}{5}}{1 - \frac{1}{25}} = \tan^{-1}\frac{5}{12}$.
Step 2: $\tan\left(\theta - \frac{\pi}{4}\right) = \frac{\tan\theta - 1}{1 + \tan\theta} = \frac{\frac{5}{12} - 1}{1 + \frac{5}{12}} = \frac{-\frac{7}{12}}{\frac{17}{12}}$.
Step 3: Value $= -\frac{7}{17}$.
Final Answer: (C) $\frac{-7}{17}$
Quick Tip: $2\tan^{-1}\frac{1}{5} < \frac{\pi}{4}$, so the answer must be negative.

questions.stem: If $X \sim B(35, p)$ such that $7P(X = 0) = P(X = 1)$ then the value of $\frac{P(X = 15)}{P(X = 20)}$ is equal to
questions.solution:
Step 1: $7q^{35} = 35pq^{34} \Rightarrow 7q = 35p \Rightarrow q = 5p$. With $p + q = 1$: $p = \frac{1}{6}$, $q = \frac{5}{6}$.
Step 2: $\frac{P(X = 15)}{P(X = 20)} = \frac{{}^{35}C_{15}p^{15}q^{20}}{{}^{35}C_{20}p^{20}q^{15}} = \left(\frac{q}{p}\right)^{5}$, since ${}^{35}C_{15} = {}^{35}C_{20}$.
Step 3: $\left(\frac{q}{p}\right)^{5} = 5^{5} = 3125$.
Final Answer: (B) 3125
Quick Tip: Only the ratio $\frac{q}{p}$ is needed; it comes straight from $7P(0) = P(1)$.

questions.stem:
A student studies for X number of hours during a randomly selected school day. The probability that X can take the values, has the following form, where k is some constant.
$P(X = x) = \begin{cases} 0.2, & \text{if } x = 0 \\ kx, & \text{if } x = 1 \text{ or } 2 \\ k(6 - x), & \text{if } x = 3 \text{ or } 4 \\ 0, & \text{otherwise} \end{cases}$
The probability that the student studies for at most two hours is
questions.solution:
Step 1: Probabilities: $P(0) = 0.2$, $P(1) = k$, $P(2) = 2k$, $P(3) = 3k$, $P(4) = 2k$.
Step 2: Total $= 0.2 + 8k = 1 \Rightarrow k = 0.1$.
Step 3: $P(X \leq 2) = 0.2 + 0.1 + 0.2 = 0.5$.
Final Answer: (B) 0.5
Quick Tip: Always find $k$ from the total probability $= 1$ first.
